messages:
lina: Quick postmortem follow-up from the latency spike on Thursday — I want to capture owners/timelines for the remaining remediation items and make the SLO/SLA changes explicit.
sam: thanks — adding context: p95 spiked ~2.1s for ~18 minutes, throughput dropped briefly. ops-bot posted the timeline.
ops-bot: Incident summary: 2024-11-14 02:05-02:23 UTC | p95 latency 2.1s | error rate stayed <0.1% | automatic fallback to smaller model triggered at 02:10
noah: I sketched a proposal: tighten p95 SLO alert to 1.2s for the hosted tier, keep SLA at 1.5s but add a throughput window check. Thoughts?
rachel: that sounds aggressive for some customers — maybe make the alert target 1.3s and tier it by customer class? we should also add a dashboard panel for sustained throughput drop (5min avg < 60% expected)
lina: action list I'm creating (please react with :thumbsup: if you accept):
- A1: investigate root cause of 02:10 fallback spike (owner: @noah) — timeline: reproduce/initial findings by EOD tomorrow
- A2: add a new p95-by-model dashboard with 1m and 5m rollups (owner: @rachel) — timeline: 3 business days
- A3: adjust alert thresholds and add SLA gating rule (owner: @sam) — timeline: proposal in 48h, rollback plan included
- A4: runbook update for fallback policy and auto-fallback thresholds (owner: @lina) — timeline: draft in 2 business days
sam: accepting A3. I'll post the alert diff in #eng-monitoring and link here. Plan: split alert into severity1 (p95>1.3s for 5m) and severity2 (p95>1.5s for 2m with throughput drop).
noah: accepting A1. First pass: check batching/kvs cache pressure, and recent kernel changes in runtime. Will post notes in this thread.
rachel: accepting A2. dashboard queries I plan to add (pseudo PromQL):
```
# p95 by model, 1m
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference",model!=""}[1m])) by (le, model))
```
and a throughput panel:
```
sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[5m])) by (deployment)
```
lina: also we should update the error budget policy: given the recent trend we consumed ~12% in the last month; propose lowering soft alert threshold from 20% to 15% and keep hard mitigation at 25%. Any objections?
samir: (note: sam is @sam) I'm fine with 15% soft. We should also add automated notifications to customers with dedicated capacity when we hit 10% consumption in a month.
noah: +1 on adding customer notifications. I'll wire the event in the monitoring pipeline once A3 is merged.
rachel: schedule check-in: can we do a 30m sync Friday 10:00am PT to close the loop after the dashboards are up? If not, propose Monday.
lina: Friday works for me. I'll create a calendar invite and include the postmortem doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/postmortems/2024-11-14-latency-spike
ops-bot: Reminder: please add the PR links to this thread when ready — tagging owners with pending items in 48h.
sam: I'll post the alert PR by EOD tomorrow and ping here.
noah: initial root-cause note posted: found higher-than-usual KV cache evictions during the window, correlates with a rollout at 02:00 UTC. digging into rollout contents.
lina: thanks all. I'll update the action tracker and check off items as we close. If anyone needs to reprioritize, ping me directly. :white_check_mark:
